standard_prerequisites.name: The inertia group of a maximal ideal in a Galois extension of a discretely valued field, and the decomposition group
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: fixed at statement lines 33477-33479 and used throughout the counted proof span
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the group I and the quotient D/I whose action on the residue field is analysed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The norm of a uniformizer and multiplicativity of ramification indices in a tower of discretely valued fields
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the two degree formulae whose comparison yields the etaleness conclusion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Purely inseparable residue extension for the invariants subgroup, and faithfulness of the action of D/I
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the bound [kappa(m') : kappa] >= |D/I| that the index comparison consumes.

core_obligations: Set B' = B^I and m' = B' cap m, and record from the definitions that B' is the integral closure of A in L^I (proof lines 33485-33487).
Use that m is the unique prime ideal of B lying over m' (proof lines 33488-33489).

Since I acts trivially on kappa(m), use the invariants-modulo lemma to conclude that kappa(m)/kappa(m') is purely inseparable, and hence that D/I acts faithfully on kappa(m); note that the residue field kappa of A is fixed by this action (proof lines 33490-33498).
Apply Galois theory to obtain [kappa(m') : kappa] >= |D/I| (proof lines 33499-33500).

For a uniformizer pi of A, use Norm_{L/K}(pi) = pi^{[L:K]} to derive the displayed identity |G| = [L:K] = |G/D| [kappa(m):kappa] ord_{B_m}(pi), using that there are |G/D| maximal ideals of B, all conjugate (proof lines 33503-33514).
Apply the same reasoning to the extension L/L^I of degree |I| to obtain |I| ord_{B'_{m'}}(pi) = [kappa(m):kappa(m')] ord_{B_m}(pi) (proof lines 33515-33520 and following).

Combine the two degree formulae with the Galois-theoretic bound to conclude that the ramification index of the local extension is 1 and the residue extension is separable, which says precisely that A -> (B^I)_{B^I cap m} is etale (statement conclusion).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K, a finite Galois extension L/K, a maximal ideal m of the integral closure B of A in L, and the inertia group I of m, and asserts that B^I is the integral closure of A in L^I and that A -> (B^I)_{B^I cap m} is etale (source lines 33474-33482). The proof is a genuine index computation. It writes B' = B^I and m' = B' cap m, uses that m is the unique prime of B over m', and notes that since I acts trivially on kappa(m) the extension kappa(m)/kappa(m') is purely inseparable, so D/I acts faithfully on kappa(m'); then Galois theory gives [kappa(m') : kappa] >= |D/I| (proof lines 33485-33500). The substantive part is a numerical comparison of the two degree formulae: using that Norm_{L/K}(pi) = pi^{[L:K]} one gets |G| = [L:K] = |G/D| [kappa(m):kappa] ord_{B_m}(pi), and applying the same reasoning to L/L^I of degree |I| gives |I| ord_{B'_{m'}}(pi) = [kappa(m):kappa(m')] ord_{B_m}(pi) (proof lines 33502-33520 and following). Combining these with the Galois-theoretic bound on [kappa(m'):kappa] forces the ramification index of the local extension to be 1 and the residue extension to be separable, which is exactly etaleness. The non-routine content is the interplay of the ramification-index multiplicativity, the norm formula for the uniformizer and the bound coming from faithfulness of the action of D/I on the residue field.
